steps.say: This lesson walks through a first change, changing a theme. It types only into its own scratch copy in prism-lesson/, which goes away when the lesson ends. Every real file stays as it is.
The starter themes are here, one Facet file each. A theme is a finished desktop the companion can start from and make the person's own.
This is Calm, the real one. Only look at it here.
Every theme takes its colours, fonts and corners from these variables. To recolour a theme, change them, not each rule.
Here is the lesson's copy of the beginning of Calm. All the typing happens in this file.
A rule written later wins. One more line gives the accent a warm red. The companion's own small edits work the same way.
Structure is markup. A second clock with a different format shows the day of the week under the time.
**Ctrl+S** saves. Until then the change is only on screen.
The git view lists what changed. The lesson's scratch file shows here too, until the lesson ends. Check this list before every commit.

How a real theme edit reaches the OS: everything under userland/rootfs is copied into the initrd, the archive the kernel unpacks at boot. So the change shows only after a new image, such as `make dev-iso`.

steps.say: If you **add** a theme rather than change one, its name must be added here as well. The companion's instructions list the themes by name; this list is not read from the folder.

steps.say: Words in the OS's own screens live in C. This is a Settings row: a name and a line under it. To change what a row says, change the text between the quotes, then rebuild os-shell.
Either way, the steps are the same: find the real place, change as little as you can, and check it. Next: **14 Checking a change**.
